name: Fertiliser supply
value: Egypt urea ~$535/t; gas cuts up to 33%
summary: Egyptian urea near $535 a tonne as gas cuts to fertiliser plants deepen to as much as 33%; Gulf supply still curbed
state: Egyptian granular urea fetched about $535 a tonne FOB for November, up about 17% from September, and gas curtailments to fertiliser plants rose from 20% on 1 Nov to as much as 33%, which is expected to throttle exports (EnterpriseAM, 9 Nov). The Gulf supplies about a third of world urea exports, and about 3.9 million tonnes a year were suspended at the peak of the Hormuz disruption, according to IFPRI (Global Agriculture, 30 Oct). Gulf shipments continue at reduced volumes and no 60% three-month rise in urea was found, so Watch holds.
for_you: Higher fertiliser costs tend to squeeze farm margins and can feed into food prices next season. Farmers buying for spring application are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Watch: supply from major exporters curtailed (Egypt gas cuts, Gulf exports down); urea +17% in 2 months, below 60% Alert line

sources.title: Gov't deepens industrial gas rationing, raising curtailments on fertilizer and methanol plants to 33%
Fertiliser Costs Stay High As Hormuz Conflict Drags Into Ninth Month

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
